items.issuing_body: CFTC (Commodity Futures Trading Commission)
items.title: CFTC invokes emergency authority to stay KalshiEX's own rule change and orders fulfillment of Michigan-resident trades — first federal override targeting a DCM's state-court-directed rule amendment
items.facts: On July 14, 2026, the CFTC issued Press Release 9267-26, announcing it had exercised emergency authority under the Commodity Exchange Act to stay a KalshiEX rule change and order KalshiEX to fulfill pending trades. Background: a Michigan state court issued a temporary restraining order directing KalshiEX to cancel all executed trades by Michigan-resident customers; KalshiEX filed an emergency rule change with the CFTC to comply with that state court order. The CFTC stayed the KalshiEX rule change and ordered KalshiEX to fulfill all pending trades per normal exchange practices. CFTC Chairman Brian Quintenz Selig stated the action was 'unprecedented,' noting Michigan is 'the first state to attempt to directly interfere with already-executed transactions on a federally regulated exchange.' As of the release, the CFTC has filed preemption suits against nine states: Arizona, Connecticut, Illinois, Kentucky, Minnesota, New Mexico, New York, Rhode Island, and Wisconsin.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9267-26 (July 14, 2026)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, CFTC-registered entities (DCMs, FCMs, DCOs), event-contract operators, sportsbooks, state gaming regulators

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate / Senate Banking & Agriculture Committees (via staff)
items.title: CLARITY Act: Senate staff expected to release unified crypto market-structure draft this week; floor vote targeted July 20; August 7 recess is the hard deadline — passage odds at 50%
items.facts: Multiple credible outlets (crypto.news, TechTimes, The Hill) reported on July 11-12, 2026 that Senate staff are expected to release a unified draft of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633) during the week of July 13, 2026, merging parallel Senate Banking and Agriculture Committee texts. Floor action is targeted for the week of July 20. The Senate leaves for its August recess on August 7, 2026, leaving approximately three working weeks. Galaxy Research has reduced 2026 passage odds to 50%, citing calendar compression, down from 60% earlier in July. Three disputes remain unresolved: (1) ethics/conflict-of-interest rules covering senior officials with crypto holdings; (2) CFTC commissioner vacancies; (3) Section 604 blockchain developer shield. H.R. 3633 passed the House 294-134 on July 17, 2025; cleared Senate Banking Committee 15-9 on May 14, 2026; placed on Senate Calendar No. 423 on June 1, 2026.
items.source_label: crypto.news via Cryptonews.net — 'Three weeks to 2030: the seven-Democrat math that decides the CLARITY Act', July 11 2026 (corroborated by TechTimes July 12 and The Hill July 1)
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, digital-asset operators, DeFi builders, token issuers, fintech operators, institutional investors

items.issuing_body: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
items.title: SEC regulatory agenda targets July 2026 for three crypto rulemakings (digital-asset offerings, broker-dealer custody, market structure)
items.facts: Per The Cryptonomist (July 11, 2026) citing the SEC's RegInfo Unified Agenda, the Securities and Exchange Commission has set July 2026 targets for three crypto rule proposals: (1) digital-asset offerings — a Division of Corporation Finance rulemaking that may include exemptions or safe harbors (legal authority listed as 'not yet determined'); (2) broker-dealer financial-responsibility, custody, and recordkeeping amendments (Rules 15c3-1, 15c3-3, 17a-3, 17a-4); and (3) market-structure amendments for crypto trading venues. As of July 11, 2026, no proposal had appeared in the Federal Register; the RegInfo entries reflect agenda-stage targets, not filed NPRMs. Corroborated by Decrypt, The Industry Spread, and Yahoo Finance.
items.source_label: The Cryptonomist (July 11, 2026), citing the SEC RegInfo Unified Agenda; corroborated by Decrypt, The Industry Spread, Yahoo Finance
items.relevant_to: crypto token issuers, broker-dealers, digital-asset custodians, crypto trading venues, exchanges

items.issuing_body: OCC / FDIC / NCUA / U.S. Treasury / FinCEN / OFAC
items.title: GENIUS Act stablecoin rulemaking deadline (July 18, 2026) one week out — six agencies had not finalized implementing rules as of July 11
items.facts: As of July 11, 2026, six federal agencies — the OCC, FDIC, NCUA, U.S. Treasury, FinCEN, and OFAC — faced a statutory July 18, 2026 deadline (one year after the GENIUS Act's July 18, 2025 enactment) to finalize implementing rules for permitted payment stablecoin issuers (PPSIs), and had not yet issued final rules. Comment periods on the proposed rules closed by early June 2026. The proposed framework requires PPSIs to hold 1:1 reserves in cash, insured deposits, and short-term U.S. Treasuries, and treats issuers as financial institutions under the Bank Secrecy Act. Source: Tech Times (July 11, 2026); corroborated by CryptoSlate and rulemaking trackers (Chapman & Cutler, Paradigm).
items.source_label: Tech Times (July 11, 2026); corroborated by CryptoSlate and rulemaking trackers
items.relevant_to: payment stablecoin issuers, banks and credit unions entering stablecoins, digital-asset custodians, BSA/AML compliance teams

items.issuing_body: Arizona Department of Gaming
items.title: Arizona Department of Gaming serves cease-and-desist orders on five online gambling operators, alleging felony money laundering and gambling promotion
items.facts: On July 10, 2026, the Arizona Department of Gaming (ADG) issued cease-and-desist orders to BetOpenly, Bookmaker, Club WPT Online Poker, Kutt Inc., and Raffle Creator. Each order alleges three Arizona felonies under A.R.S. Title 13, Chapter 33: (1) promotion of gambling, (2) illegal control of an enterprise, and (3) money laundering. ADG additionally alleged underage gambling (under-21 access) at BetOpenly, Club WPT Online Poker, and Raffle Creator; commission-based peer-to-peer wagering (prohibited under Arizona social-gambling law) at BetOpenly and Kutt Inc.; and unlicensed horse racing, casino, and sports betting at Bookmaker; and online poker (illegal in Arizona) at Club WPT. All five are directed to immediately cease all gambling operations in Arizona. Future actions may include criminal charges, civil suits, restitution, and forfeiture. ADG Director Jackie Johnson stated: 'Arizona is taking decisive action against illegal gambling operators that put Arizonans at risk.' This action expands ADG's 2025 sweepstakes-casino enforcement pattern to peer-to-peer wagering platforms, offshore sportsbooks, and unlicensed poker operators.
items.source_label: Arizona Department of Gaming — Press Release, July 10 2026
items.relevant_to: online gaming operators with Arizona users; peer-to-peer wagering platforms; offshore sportsbooks; unlicensed poker platforms

items.issuing_body: U.S. Congress (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, H.R.6644 §1101)
items.title: First U.S. statutory ban on a Federal Reserve CBDC takes effect via the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R.6644 §1101)
items.facts: On July 10, 2026, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R.6644) became law without President Trump's signature. Per coverage by The Cryptonomist (July 10, 2026), corroborated by Tech Times (July 11, 2026) and CoinDesk (July 9-10, 2026), Section 1101 prohibits the Federal Reserve from issuing a central bank digital currency (CBDC) or any substantially similar digital asset through December 31, 2030. The bill passed the Senate 85-5 (June 22) and the House 358-32. Coverage reports a carve-out for open, permissionless, privately issued dollar-denominated digital assets (understood to include stablecoins). Statutory text cited by coverage but not independently retrieved. Follows the Senate-passage entry (2026-06-19-senate-passes-road-housing-cbdc-ban) and bill-text entry (2026-06-18-congress-cbdc-ban-road-to-housing-act).
items.source_label: The Cryptonomist (July 10, 2026); corroborated by Tech Times (July 11, 2026) and CoinDesk (July 9-10, 2026); statute text not independently retrieved
items.relevant_to: stablecoin issuers, payment and fintech platforms, banks, digital-dollar infrastructure providers

items.issuing_body: OCC (Office of the Comptroller of the Currency)
items.title: OCC grants Circle final approval for a national trust bank charter (First National Digital Currency Bank, N.A. / Circle National Trust)
items.facts: On July 10, 2026, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted Circle Internet Group final approval to establish First National Digital Currency Bank, N.A. (operating as Circle National Trust), a national trust bank that will provide fiduciary digital-asset custody for Circle and its affiliates. Circle applied to the OCC on June 30, 2025 and received conditional approval in December 2025 before final approval on July 10, 2026. As reported, this is the first national trust bank charter granted to a stablecoin issuer. Source: Circle press release (July 10, 2026); corroborated by American Banker, CoinDesk, CNBC, and BusinessWire. OCC decision letter not independently retrieved.
items.source_label: Circle Press Release (July 10, 2026); corroborated by American Banker, CoinDesk, CNBC, BusinessWire; OCC decision letter not independently retrieved
items.relevant_to: stablecoin issuers, digital-asset custodians, national trust banks, crypto-native firms pursuing federal charters

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate (Banking Committee / Agriculture Committee)
items.title: Merged Senate CLARITY Act draft expected week of July 20; ethics provision remains the sticking point; no text filed as of July 9
items.facts: CoinDesk reported (July 9, 2026) that a new merged version of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act — combining Senate Banking and Agriculture Committee texts, with reportedly more than 70 pages added — could be released as soon as the week of July 20, 2026 for potential Senate floor action. Per the reporting, the draft had not secured the Democratic support needed for 60 votes to clear a filibuster; the main open issue was an ethics provision restricting senior officials, including the president, from crypto business ties, with federal preemption rules and SEC/CFTC commissioner nominations also unresolved. No bill text had been filed as of July 9, 2026.
items.source_label: CoinDesk (July 9, 2026)
items.relevant_to: crypto market-structure stakeholders, exchanges, token issuers, CFTC/SEC-regulated venues, DeFi protocols

items.issuing_body: North Carolina Office of the Governor
items.title: North Carolina Governor Stein signs $34B SB 257 budget enacting 6% prediction-market tax on net trading-fee revenue, effective 2027
items.facts: On July 8, 2026, North Carolina Governor Josh Stein signed Senate Bill 257, the state's approximately $34 billion fiscal year 2026 budget. As reported by GamblingNews (July 8, 2026), the enacted budget includes a 6% tax on the net trading fee revenue earned by prediction market operators with North Carolina users; platforms named in reporting include Kalshi and Polymarket. The tax is scheduled to take effect in 2027. The enacted budget does not impose state gambling licensing, know-your-customer, or responsible-gaming requirements on prediction-market platforms. This item supersedes the July 6 item (2026-07-06-north-carolina-prediction-market-tax), which covered SB 257 at conference committee stage; the Governor's signing converts it to enacted law.
items.source_label: GamblingNews (July 8, 2026; reporting the Governor's signing of SB 257)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, sports-betting operators, tax and compliance teams serving operators with North Carolina users

items.issuing_body: New Jersey Senate Budget and Appropriations Committee
items.title: New Jersey Senate Budget Committee approves amended S4447 (9% prediction-market gross income tax) 9-4; amended bill explicitly recognizes CFTC as federal regulator
items.facts: As reported by GamblingNews (July 8, 2026), the New Jersey Senate Budget and Appropriations Committee approved amendments to S4447 by a 9-4 vote. The amended bill imposes a 9% tax on prediction market gross income for operators offering event contracts to New Jersey residents. The amended version explicitly recognizes the CFTC as the federal regulator of prediction markets and drops prior self-exclusion requirements. The New Jersey Office of Legislative Services estimated the tax would generate approximately $10.3 million to $15.3 million annually. The bill requires a full Senate vote, Assembly action, and the Governor's signature before becoming law.
items.source_label: GamblingNews (July 8, 2026; reporting the Committee vote on S4447)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, tax and compliance teams, payment processors serving operators with New Jersey users

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate (Senate Banking Committee markup; Senate Legislative Calendar No. 423) / House Agriculture digital-assets subcommittee (Rep. Dusty Johnson statement)
items.title: CLARITY Act placed on Senate Legislative Calendar No. 423; House Agriculture chair commits to fast follow; August recess is the operative deadline; seven Democratic votes remain the gap to cloture
items.facts: The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act has been placed on the U.S. Senate Legislative Calendar as Calendar No. 423, following a 15-9 Senate Banking Committee markup on May 14, 2026. House Agriculture digital-assets subcommittee chair Rep. Dusty Johnson stated the House will move immediately on a companion measure if the Senate passes the bill before the August recess. The bill requires approximately 60 votes to clear a Senate filibuster — about seven Democratic votes beyond full Republican unity.
items.source_label: The Defiant (June 19, 2026; corroborated by PYMNTS.com, Yahoo Finance, CoinPedia, and Seeking Alpha)
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, digital-asset market participants, stablecoin issuers, prediction-market platforms, brokerages, DeFi protocols, fintech companies

items.issuing_body: American Gaming Association, Indian Gaming Association, AFL-CIO Hotel and Gaming Trades Council, UNITE HERE (coalition letter to U.S. Senate, June 16, 2026)
items.title: AGA, tribal gaming groups, and labor unions send Senate letter demanding CLARITY Act include explicit ban on prediction-market sports event contracts
items.facts: On June 16, 2026, a coalition led by the AGA, the Indian Gaming Association, the AFL-CIO's Hotel and Gaming Trades Council, and UNITE HERE sent a letter to the U.S. Senate urging legislators to amend the CLARITY Act to include explicit language barring prediction markets from offering sports and casino-style event contracts. The AGA has separately estimated states have lost roughly $1 billion in gaming tax revenue to prediction markets since the start of 2025.
items.source_label: The Defiant (June 17, 2026; corroborated by CryptoNews, AMBCrypto, Sportsbook Review, Yogonet, BanklessTimes, and Covers.com)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market operators, gaming operators, tribal gaming entities, sportsbooks, CFTC-registered entities

items.issuing_body: CFTC — U.S. District Court, Northern District of Illinois
items.title: CFTC amends its Illinois lawsuit and seeks a preliminary injunction against the state's new 'exchange wager' prediction-market tax
items.facts: The CFTC amended its lawsuit against the State of Illinois (N.D. Illinois, No. 1:26-cv-03659) after Gov. JB Pritzker signed a budget creating a new tax structure for prediction markets. The amended complaint challenges Illinois's 'exchange wager' provisions imposing transaction fees of 1.75% to 3.5% on sports event contracts. The CFTC also filed a motion for a preliminary injunction.
items.source_label: Gambling Insider (June 19, 2026 weekly roundup)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market / event-contract platforms, crypto derivatives exchanges, CFTC registrants, tax and compliance teams

items.issuing_body: Matthew Mazza (plaintiff) — U.S. District Court, Northern District of California
items.title: Proposed class action alleges Robinhood runs an unlicensed sports-gambling operation through its prediction-markets hub
items.facts: On June 10, 2026, a proposed class action (Mazza v. Robinhood) was filed in the N.D. California against Robinhood Markets, Inc. and Robinhood Derivatives, alleging the company operates an unlicensed, illegal sports-gambling operation. The named plaintiff alleges he lost approximately $400,000 in fees, commissions, and wagers in 2025-2026.

items.issuing_body: Cayuga Nation (plaintiff) — U.S. District Court, Northern District of New York
items.title: Cayuga Nation sues Caesars Sportsbook over mobile bets placed on tribal land — first tribal lawsuit against licensed sportsbook; novel IGRA 'where is the bet placed' geolocation theory
items.facts: On June 16, 2026, the Cayuga Nation of New York filed a federal lawsuit against American Wagering, Inc. (d/b/a Caesars Sportsbook), alleging that Caesars accepted mobile sports wagers from people physically located on the Cayuga reservation without tribal authorization, a gaming compact, or federal oversight, in violation of IGRA.
items.source_label: Casino.org (Philip Conneller, June 18, 2026; confirmed by fingerlakes1.com, SBC Americas, BettorsInsider, CasinoBeats, CDC Gaming, iGamingToday)

items.issuing_body: U.S. Senate
items.title: U.S. Senate passes 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644) with statutory Fed CBDC ban through 2030; House concurrence vote pending
items.facts: On June 18, 2026, the U.S. Senate invoked cloture (84-8) and passed H.R. 6644. The bill includes a provision banning the Federal Reserve from issuing or creating a CBDC through December 31, 2030. The amended bill returns to the House for concurrence.

items.issuing_body: U.S. District Court, W.D. Michigan (Judge Paul Maloney)
items.title: W.D. Michigan denies Robinhood preliminary injunction — sports event contracts are NOT swaps; CEA does not clearly preempt state gambling law
items.facts: On June 18, 2026, U.S. District Judge Paul Maloney denied Robinhood's motion for a preliminary injunction against Michigan state gambling enforcement. The court held: (1) sports event contracts are not 'swaps' under the CEA; and (2) even if they were swaps, it is not clearly established that the CEA would preempt Michigan's state gambling law.
items.source_label: Gambling Insider (June 18, 2026; corroborated by Decrypt)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market operators, event-contract platforms, brokerages offering sports contracts, state gaming regulators

items.issuing_body: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
items.title: Sixth Circuit denies CFTC motion to participate as amicus at oral argument in KalshiEx v. Schuler (No. 26-3196)
items.facts: On June 16, 2026, the Sixth Circuit denied the CFTC's motion to appear as amicus curiae at oral argument in KalshiEx LLC v. Matthew T. Schuler et al. (No. 26-3196). The CFTC had submitted a written amicus brief on May 12, 2026, asserting exclusive CFTC jurisdiction over prediction markets.

items.issuing_body: Federal Reserve, OCC, FDIC, NCUA, and Treasury (FinCEN)
items.title: Five federal agencies propose a customer identification program rule for payment stablecoin issuers (GENIUS Act)
items.facts: On June 18, 2026, the Federal Reserve Board — jointly with the OCC, FDIC, NCUA, and Treasury/FinCEN — requested comment on a proposed rule requiring permitted payment stablecoin issuers (PPSIs) to maintain an effective customer identification program (CIP). Comments are due 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.
items.source_label: Federal Reserve Board Press Release (June 18, 2026); joint with OCC, FDIC, NCUA, and Treasury/FinCEN.
items.relevant_to: payment stablecoin issuers (PPSIs), crypto exchanges and custodians, banks and credit unions entering stablecoins, BSA/AML and compliance teams

items.issuing_body: State of Illinois (Gov. JB Pritzker)
items.title: Illinois enacts first-in-nation digital-asset transaction tax (SB 3019 / Digital Asset Tax Act)
items.facts: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed Senate Bill 3019, the Digital Asset Tax Act (DATA), as part of the state's $55.9 billion budget, making Illinois the first U.S. state to impose a transaction-based tax on digital-asset activity. The law imposes a 0.2% privilege tax on brokers who exchange, transfer, or store digital assets for customers in the state; takes effect January 1, 2027.
items.source_label: Crypto Briefing (reporting Illinois SB 3019; signing also reported by Yahoo Finance, Bitcoin Magazine, The Defiant)
items.relevant_to: crypto exchanges, brokers, custodians and wallet providers with Illinois nexus; payment processors; tax/compliance teams

items.facts: A coalition of federally recognized tribes filed amicus briefs in two federal prediction-market cases, arguing that allowing Kalshi and the CFTC to override state gaming laws would also nullify tribal-state gaming compacts.

items.facts: On June 18, 2026, the CFTC entered a final consent order against Celsius Network LLC and its former CEO Alex Mashinsky resolving: (1) fraudulent misrepresentation; (2) market manipulation of the CEL token; and (3) operating as an unregistered commodity pool operator. The DOJ's separate criminal case against Mashinsky continues.

This is the first joint inter-agency RFI on the jurisdictional classification of event contracts and prediction markets.

items.facts: CME Group filed suit against the CFTC challenging the June 2026 approval of Bitcoin perpetual futures contracts (BTCPERP) on KalshiEx via Regulation 40.2 self-certification. items.title: Delaware (HB 441) and New Jersey (S-2141) advance statewide crypto-ATM bans
items.facts: Delaware and New Jersey have each advanced legislation to ban cryptocurrency ATMs statewide, citing fraud losses. Delaware's HB 441 passed the House; it would require existing kiosks to go dark upon enactment and be physically removed within 90 days. New Jersey's S-2141 cleared the Senate Commerce Committee unanimously.
items.source_label: The Defiant (reporting the Delaware and New Jersey crypto-ATM ban bills)
items.relevant_to: crypto-ATM/kiosk operators, payment processors, compliance vendors

items.title: Fintech trade group sues Tennessee to block remittance tax (HB2502)
items.facts: The Financial Technology Association filed suit in Davidson County (Tennessee) Chancery Court seeking an injunction to block HB2502, a law signed by Gov. Bill Lee in May 2026 that adds a $10 fee on monetary wire transfers abroad plus a 2% tax on transfers over $500 (effective Jan. 1, 2027). The FTA argues the law is unconstitutional under the dormant Commerce Clause.
items.source_label: The Center Square (reporting the FTA v. Tennessee filing)
items.relevant_to: money transmitters, remittance providers, payment processors, fintechs

items.issuing_body: CFTC
items.title: CFTC sues New Mexico over prediction-market preemption (8th state)
items.facts: On 2026-06-12 the CFTC filed suit against the State of New Mexico, seeking a declaratory judgment that federal law grants it exclusive authority over event contracts and a permanent injunction barring the state from enforcing preempted gaming laws against CFTC registrants. New Mexico joins AZ, CT, IL, NY, MN, RI, and WI.
items.source_label: CFTC Press Release 9251-26
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, sportsbooks, exchanges, CFTC registrants

items.issuing_body: Nevada Gaming Control Board
items.title: Nevada gaming regulator seeks to hold Kalshi in contempt over prediction-market geofencing
items.facts: On 2026-06-12 the Nevada Gaming Control Board petitioned the First Judicial District Court in Carson City to find KalshiEx LLC in contempt for allegedly not complying with a May 18 order requiring it to geofence its website so it cannot offer sports-, election-, or entertainment-related event contracts to anyone located in Nevada.
items.source_label: Las Vegas Review-Journal (reporting the Nevada GCB court filing)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, geolocation/compliance vendors, sportsbooks

items.issuing_body: Coalition for Fair Markets (NADEX, Kalshi, Polymarket/QCX)
items.title: Prediction-market coalition sues Kentucky over 14.25% tax on event-contract trading
items.facts: On 2026-06-12, the Coalition for Fair Markets — comprising Crypto.com's NADEX, Kalshi, and Polymarket's U.S. exchange QCX — filed suit in Franklin Circuit Court to block Kentucky from implementing a 14.25% tax on prediction-market transaction fees set to take effect Jan. 1, 2027.
items.source_label: SBC Americas (reporting the Coalition for Fair Markets filing; first reported by the Associated Press)
items.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, licensed gaming operators, payment processors
